rv.q: This absorbing revival of Ryan Craig's play from 2011 is also an unravelling, one in which morality and geopolitics play out.
While still set in 2009, the play feels bracingly relevant.
Time and again, you find yourself laughing through the pain while admiring the finely wrought performances from a cast led by Tracy-Ann Oberman.
This is a serious, and at times seriously funny, bid to show how events in Gaza impact Jews elsewhere, but also a clumsy one.
Strong performances hold together this knotty, overstuffed drama
The trouble is that for all its bracing relevance, the Israel/Gaza stuff is so bombastic as to overwhelm the more nuanced family tragedy.
What The Holy Rosenbergs lacks in escapism, it more than makes up for in its thought-provoking nature.
The Holy Rosenbergs is a powerful reminder that an excellent piece of new writing is news that stays news.
The Holy Rosenbergs remains a sturdy, occasionally engaging examination of family, faith and political conscience.
